behavior: POST /signup rejects a request from an IP that has already made 5 signups in the trailing 60 minutes with 429 Too Many Requests; the counter is stored in Redis with a sliding TTL keyed by IP, not in-process memory (so it survives a process restart and works across multiple app instances)

layers.label: Layer 1 — Syntax & Static
layers.repair: Run 'make lint' and fix each reported violation.

layers.label: Layer 2 — Runtime Behavior
layers.repair: If the 6th request in a window isn't rejected: check the Redis key TTL is being reset correctly (INCR + EXPIRE, not EXPIRE-only). If it's rejecting on cold start: check the counter defaults to 0, not undefined, on the first request from a new IP.

layers.label: Layer 3 — Multi-instance behavior
layers.cmd: docker compose -f docker-compose.test.yml up -d && sleep 2 && pytest tests/test_rate_limit_distributed.py -v; code=$?; docker compose -f docker-compose.test.yml down; exit $code
layers.repair: If the limit resets between requests routed to different app instances: the counter is probably in-process (e.g. a plain dict) instead of the shared Redis store — grep for any in-memory fallback and remove it.

notes: Limit and window are configurable via SIGNUP_RATE_LIMIT and SIGNUP_RATE_WINDOW_SECONDS env vars, defaulting to 5/3600. Do not hardcode either value in the handler.

behavior: Admin dashboard's 'Export users' button streams a CSV of all users (id, email, created_at, plan) without loading the full table into memory — must handle a 500k-row table without the request timing out or the process OOMing

layers.label: Layer 1 — Syntax & Static
layers.repair: Run 'make lint' and fix reported violations.

layers.label: Layer 2 — Runtime Behavior
layers.repair: If memory usage spikes in the test: confirm the export uses a server-side cursor / chunked query (e.g. yield_per()) rather than .all() on the full queryset.

layers.label: Layer 3 — Real deploy confirmation
layers.cmd: gh run list --branch main --limit 1 --json conclusion,name -q '.[] | select(.name == "Deploy") | .conclusion' | grep -q success
layers.repair: This layer checks that the most recent Deploy workflow run on main succeeded — it does not re-run the export itself. If it fails, check the Actions tab for the real failure before assuming this feature's code is at fault; it may be an unrelated deploy break that needs its own fix first.

notes: Layer 3 is deliberately a check against GitHub Actions' own run history, not prose like 'deploy and confirm it works manually' — see DECISIONS.example.md for why a human-only instruction can never legitimately pass through verify-feature.sh's eval-based layers.

behavior: When a webhook delivery fails (non-2xx or timeout), the worker retries with exponential backoff (1m, 5m, 30m, 2h, 12h) up to 5 attempts, then marks the delivery as 'dead' and surfaces it in the admin dashboard's Failed Deliveries tab
notes: Blocked on F02's export infra — the Failed Deliveries tab reuses the same streaming-table component F02 introduces. Do not start the Planner/Verifier steps for F03 until F02 reaches 'passing'.
